ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $63.10 surge differential to the rider's original payment method and issue the driver a notice-duty/communication reminder for the incomplete surge notice (surge notice omitted the rider's free-cancellation right).
ruling.reasoning:
No safety issue: the only chats are pickup logistics [F10][F11]; the driver's statement [F13] contains no threat, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation. Safety screen clear.

Route is clean: actual distance equals the optimal route, +0.0 km [F1][F3], so there is no deviation and RD-1/RD-2 are not engaged. The whole $63.10 gap between the $71.67 quote [F6] and the $134.77 charged [F5][F7] is attributable to the surge multiplier rising from 1× to 2× at trip start [F4][F8], i.e. a SURGE-1/SURGE-2 case, not a route case.

Notice check under SURGE-1: the quote was binding at 1× [F6]; the multiplier rose to 2× before departure. The in-app notice was sent at 14:06:25, before the 14:09:00 trip start [F9], so the timing is good, and it stated the new multiplier (2.0×) and the revised estimated fare ($141.87) [F9]. But the third required item — that the rider may cancel without penalty — is missing; instead the notice says "Cancellation fees may apply" [F9], which is not a free-cancel statement. Missing any item → not notified (SURGE-1). The rider's own account ("I did not dare cancel") is consistent with that reading.

Outcome under SURGE-2: surge rose, rider not notified → refund the full surge differential. Per SURGE-3/F8 the differential is bounded by the amount the fare exceeds the quote: (2 − 1) × $66.65 = $66.65, capped at $63.10. Refund $63.10; the $1.47 booking fee is surge-exempt and not part of the differential [F7]. Amount is under $10… well under $50, so TH-1/TH-2 let the system decide; no deviation, so no RD-6 flag, and the driver's two upheld disputes are route-0/no-show-0 [F15], precluding an RD-6 flag anyway. The rider's clean profile [F14] and the driver's are consistent with the fare-only reading.

element_findings.element: Surge notice states the new multiplier
element_findings.reason: Notice text names '2.0×', which is the multiplier in effect at trip start [F4][F9].

element_findings.element: Surge notice states the revised estimated fare
Surge notice states the rider may cancel without penalty
element_findings.reason: Notice says 'Cancellation fees may apply' [F9]; that is not a statement of a free-cancellation right, so the notice is incomplete and the rider is treated as not notified under SURGE-1.

element_findings.element: Surge differential basis (whole gap from surge)
element_findings.reason: Quote $71.67 at 1×, charged $134.77 at 2×; surge component (2−1) × $66.65 = $66.65, capped at the $63.10 excess over the quote, booking fee $1.47 not surged [F5][F6][F7][F8].

rejected_claims.reason: Ryde's position that the notice was sufficient fails: SURGE-1 requires the free-cancellation option to be stated, and 'cancellation fees may apply' [F9] is the opposite.
The driver's statement [F13] does not bear on the surge-notice duty; pricing errors and notice failures remain Ryde's obligation, and the driver gives no notice evidence anyway.
